translation_en: Abu Hurairah reported that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “Whoever accuses his slave of adultery will be punished on the Day of Resurrection, unless the accusation is true.” The chain is Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Numayr, Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Numayr, Fudayl ibn Ghazwan, Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Niam, and Abu Hurairah.

This is the same report through Abu Kurayb from Waki and Zuhayr ibn Harb from Ishaq ibn Yusuf al-Azraq, both from Fudayl ibn Ghazwan. Their versions say, “I heard Abu al-Qasim, the Prophet of repentance.”

Al-Maarur ibn Suwayd said: “We passed by Abu Dharr at al-Rabadha. He and his servant were each wearing a similar garment. We said, ‘Abu Dharr, if you put them together, you would have a fine suit.’ He said, ‘There had been an argument between me and one of my brothers, and his mother was a non-Arab. I insulted him by referring to his mother, and he complained about me to the Prophet. When I met the Prophet, he said, “Abu Dharr, you still have traits of the pre-Islamic period.” I said, “Messenger of Allah, whoever insults men, they insult his father and mother.” He said, “Abu Dharr, you still have traits of the pre-Islamic period. They are your brothers, whom Allah has placed under your authority. Feed them from what you eat, clothe them from what you wear, and do not burden them with work beyond their ability. If you do, help them.”’”

This is the same report from Abu Dharr through several chains from al-Amash. Zuhayr’s and Abu Muawiyah’s versions add that Abu Dharr asked whether he still had traits of the pre-Islamic period at his present age, and the Prophet said yes. Isa’s version says that if a servant is given work beyond his ability, the master should sell him; Zuhayr’s says to help him; Abu Muawiyah’s includes neither addition and ends with not burdening him beyond his ability. The reports from Zuhayr and Abu Muawiyah add that Abu Dharr asked whether he still had traits of the pre-Islamic period at his present age, and the Prophet said yes. Isa’s version says that if a servant is given work beyond his ability, the master should sell him; Zuhayr’s says to help him; Abu Muawiyah’s includes neither addition.

Al-Maarur ibn Suwayd said he saw Abu Dharr and his servant wearing matching suits. Abu Dharr explained that he had insulted a man by taunting him about his non-Arab mother. The Prophet told Abu Dharr that he still had traits of the pre-Islamic period and that servants were his brothers under his authority. He instructed him to feed and clothe them as he did himself, not burden them beyond their ability, and help them if he did. The chain is Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashshar from Muhammad ibn Jafar, Shubah, Wasil al-Ahdab, and al-Maarur.

Abu Hurairah reported that the Messenger of Allah said: “A servant is entitled to his food and clothing, and he should only be assigned work he can manage.” Abu Hurairah reported that the Messenger of Allah said: “A servant is entitled to his food and clothing, and he should only be assigned work he can manage.” The chain is Abu Tahir, Ibn Wahb, Amr ibn al-Harith, Bukayr ibn al-Ashajj, Ajlan, and Abu Hurairah.

Abu Hurairah reported that the Messenger of Allah said: “When your servant has prepared your food and brings it after enduring its heat and smoke, seat him with you and let him eat. If the food is scarce, put a mouthful or two in his hand.” Dawud explained that this means one or two bites.
Ibn Umar reported that the Messenger of Allah said: “When a servant is sincere toward his master and worships Allah well, he receives a double reward.”

This is the same report through several chains from Ubayd Allah and Nafi, from Ibn Umar, with wording like Malik’s narration. The same report is transmitted through Yahya al-Qattan and Ubayd Allah; Ibn Numayr from his father; Ibn Numayr and Abu Usamah; and Ibn Wahb and Usamah. All report it from Nafi and Ibn Umar, with wording like Malik’s narration.

Abu Hurairah reported that the Messenger of Allah said: “A righteous slave receives a double reward.” Abu Hurairah swore by Him who holds his soul that, were it not for striving in Allah’s path, pilgrimage, and dutifulness to my mother, I would have loved to die as a slave. It was said that Abu Hurairah did not perform pilgrimage while his mother was alive so he could remain with her. Abu Tahir’s wording says “a righteous servant” without specifying a slave.
This is the same report through Zuhayr ibn Harb and Abu Safwan al-Umawi from Yunus and Ibn Shihab. It omits the statement beginning, “It was said to us,” and what follows.

Abu Hurairah reported that the Messenger of Allah said: “If a servant fulfills Allah’s rights and his masters’ rights, he receives a double reward.” Abu Hurairah said he told this to Kaab, who replied that a modest believer would have neither reckoning nor liability.
This is the same report through Zuhayr ibn Harb from Jarir, from al-Amash, with the same chain.

Abu Hurairah reported that the Messenger of Allah said: “How excellent it is for a servant to die while worshipping Allah well and serving his master well.” Abu Hurairah reported that the Messenger of Allah said: “How excellent it is for a slave to die while worshipping Allah well and keeping good company with his master.” The transmitters are Muhammad ibn Rafi, Abd al-Razzaq, Maamar, and Hammam ibn Munabbih.

Imran ibn Husayn reported that a man freed six slaves at the time of his death, when he had no other property. The Messenger of Allah summoned them, divided them into three groups, and drew lots. He freed two and kept four in slavery, then spoke sternly to the man. Imran ibn Husayn reported that a man freed six slaves at his death, having no other property. The Messenger summoned them, divided them into three groups, and drew lots. He freed two and left four enslaved, then spoke sternly to the man. The chain includes Ismail ibn Ulayyah, Ayyub, Abu Qilabah, Abu al-Muhallab, and Imran.

This is the same report through Qutaybah from Hammad and through Ishaq ibn Ibrahim and Ibn Abi Umar from al-Thaqafi, all from Ayyub. Hammad’s version is like Ibn Ulayyah’s. Al-Thaqafi’s says that an Ansari man made a bequest at death to free six slaves.

This is the same account through Muhammad ibn Minhal and Ahmad ibn Abdah, from Yazid ibn Zuray, Hisham ibn Hassan, Muhammad ibn Sirin, and Imran ibn Husayn. This is a similar report from Imran ibn Husayn through Muhammad ibn Minhal, Ahmad ibn Abdah, Yazid ibn Zuray, Hisham ibn Hassan, and Muhammad ibn Sirin.

Sahl ibn Abi Hathmah and Rafi ibn Khadij said that Abdullah ibn Sahl ibn Zayd and Muhayyisah ibn Masud ibn Zayd went to Khaybar and separated to attend to their affairs. Muhayyisah found Abdullah killed, buried him, and returned to the Messenger with Huwayyisah and the younger Abd al-Rahman ibn Sahl. When Abd al-Rahman tried to speak first, the Messenger said, “Let the older one speak first.” They told him of Abdullah’s killing. He asked whether fifty of them would swear and thereby claim their companion—or his killer. They said they had not witnessed it, so how could they swear? The Messenger said, “Then the Jews can clear themselves with fifty oaths.” They asked how they could accept the oaths of a disbelieving people. Seeing this, the Messenger paid the blood money himself.

Muhayyisah ibn Masud and Abdullah ibn Sahl went toward Khaybar and separated among the date palms. Abdullah was killed, and they suspected the Jews. His brother Abd al-Rahman and their cousins Huwayyisah and Muhayyisah came to the Prophet. Abd al-Rahman began speaking, although he was the youngest, and the Messenger told him to let the older men speak first. The Messenger said, “Let fifty of you swear against one of them, and he will be handed over to you.” They said they had not witnessed the killing and could not swear. He said the Jews could clear themselves with fifty oaths. They replied that they were disbelievers. The Messenger then paid the blood money himself. Sahl said a camel from that payment once kicked him in their enclosure.

This is a similar report from Sahl ibn Abi Hathmah. It says the Messenger paid the blood money himself, and it omits the detail that a camel kicked the narrator. This is a similar report from Sahl ibn Abi Hathmah. It says that the Messenger paid the blood money himself and omits the camel kicking the narrator.

This is a similar report through Sufyan ibn Uyaynah and Abd al-Wahhab al-Thaqafi from Yahya ibn Said, Bushayr ibn Yasar, and Sahl ibn Abi Hathmah. This is a similar report through Amr al-Naqid and Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, from Sufyan ibn Uyaynah and Abd al-Wahhab al-Thaqafi, both from Yahya ibn Said, Bushayr ibn Yasar, and Sahl ibn Abi Hathmah.

Bushayr ibn Yasar reported that Abdullah ibn Sahl and Muhayyisah, both Ansaris of Banu Harithah, went to Khaybar while it was under a peace agreement and its people were Jews. They separated, and Abdullah was found killed in a water hollow. His companion buried him and returned to Madinah. His brother Abd al-Rahman and the cousins Muhayyisah and Huwayyisah told the Messenger where Abdullah was killed. Bushayr reported from Companions who had met the Messenger that he asked them to swear fifty oaths and claim the killer or their companion. They said they had not witnessed it. He said the Jews could clear themselves with fifty oaths. They asked how they could accept the oaths of disbelievers. The Messenger paid the blood money himself.

Yahya ibn Yahya reported a similar account through Hushaym, Yahya ibn Said, Bushayr ibn Yasar, and Sahl. It adds that Sahl said one of the camels given as blood money kicked him in the enclosure. Yahya ibn Yahya reported through Hushaym, Yahya ibn Said, Bushayr ibn Yasar, and Sahl. It tells the story like al-Layth’s narration up to the Messenger paying the blood money. Sahl said that one camel from that payment kicked him in the enclosure.

Several Ansari men from Banu Harithah went to Khaybar because of hardship. Abdullah ibn Sahl was killed and thrown into a well or water hollow. Muhayyisah accused the Jews, who denied killing him. The Messenger asked Huwayyisah, Muhayyisah, and Abd al-Rahman whether they would swear and claim their companion’s blood. They said they had not witnessed the killing. He said the Jews could swear fifty oaths to clear themselves. They objected that they were not Muslims, so the Messenger paid one hundred camels from the charity camels. Sahl said a red camel from that payment once kicked him.

Some elders of his people reported that Abdullah ibn Sahl and Muhayyisah went to Khaybar because they were in hardship. Muhayyisah returned and said Abdullah had been killed and thrown into a well or pit. He went to the Jews and accused them, but they swore they had not killed him. Muhayyisah returned to his people. Then he, his older brother Huwayyisah, and Abd al-Rahman ibn Sahl went to the Messenger of Allah. Muhayyisah tried to speak first, but the Messenger told him to let the older man speak. Huwayyisah and then Muhayyisah spoke. The Messenger said, “Either they pay the blood money for your companion, or they announce war.” He wrote to the Jews, who replied by swearing they had not killed him. The Messenger asked Huwayyisah, Muhayyisah, and Abd al-Rahman whether they would swear and claim their companion’s blood. They said no. He then asked whether the Jews could swear for them. They replied that they were not Muslims. The Messenger paid the blood money himself and sent them one hundred camels, which were brought into their home. Sahl said a red camel from among them once kicked him.

This is the same report through several chains from Abu Salamah and Sulayman ibn Yasar, from an Ansari Companion. The Messenger upheld the oath procedure as it had existed in the pre-Islamic period. Abu Hurairah reported from the Messenger of Allah that he upheld the oath procedure as it had existed in the pre-Islamic period. It is transmitted through Abu Tahir and Harmalah, Ibn Wahb, Yunus, Ibn Shihab, Abu Salamah, Sulayman ibn Yasar, and an Ansari Companion.

This is the same report through Ibn Shihab, with the addition that the Messenger applied the oath procedure between some Ansaris who accused Jews of killing a man. This report adds that the Messenger applied the oath procedure between some Ansaris who accused Jews of killing a man. The chain is Muhammad ibn Rafi, Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Jurayj, and Ibn Shihab.

This is similar to Ibn Jurayj’s narration, through Yaqub ibn Ibrahim ibn Sad, his father, Salih, Ibn Shihab, Abu Salamah, and Sulayman ibn Yasar, reporting from some Ansaris. This is similar to Ibn Jurayj’s report through Hasan ibn Ali al-Hulwani, Yaqub ibn Ibrahim ibn Sad, his father, Salih, and Ibn Shihab, from Abu Salamah, Sulayman ibn Yasar, and some Ansaris.

Anas ibn Malik reported that people from Uraynah came to Madinah and found its climate unsuitable. The Messenger of Allah told them they could go to the charity camels and drink their milk and urine. They did so and recovered. Then they attacked the herdsmen, killed them, renounced Islam, and drove off the Messenger’s camels. The Prophet was informed and sent men after them. When they were brought back, he had their hands and feet cut off, their eyes branded, and left them on the stony plain until they died. Anas ibn Malik reported that people from Uraynah came to Madinah and found its climate unsuitable. The Messenger told them they could go to the charity camels and drink their milk and urine. They did so and recovered. Then they attacked the herdsmen, killed them, renounced Islam, and drove off the Messenger’s camels. The Prophet sent men after them. When they were brought back, he had their hands and feet cut off, their eyes branded, and left them on the stony plain until they died. The chain is Hushaym, Abd al-Aziz ibn Suhayb, Humayd, and Anas.

Anas said eight men from Ukl came to the Messenger, pledged allegiance to Islam, then found the land unhealthy and their bodies became sick. They complained, and he asked whether they would go out with the camel herder and drink the camels’ milk and urine. They agreed, drank, and recovered. They then killed the herder and drove away the camels. The Messenger sent people after them; they were caught and brought back. He ordered their hands and feet cut off, their eyes branded, and them left in the sun until they died. Ibn al-Sabbah’s version says they drove off the livestock and that their eyes were branded. Anas said eight men from Ukl came to the Messenger, pledged allegiance to Islam, then found the land unhealthy and their bodies became sick. They complained, and he asked whether they would go out with the camel herder and drink the camels’ milk and urine. They agreed, drank, and recovered. They then killed the herder and drove away the camels. The Messenger sent people after them; they were caught and brought back. He ordered their hands and feet cut off, their eyes branded, and them left in the sun until they died. Ibn al-Sabbah’s version says they drove away the livestock and that their eyes were branded. The chain is Ibn Ulayyah, Hajjaj ibn Abi Uthman, Abu Raja, Abu Qilabah, and Anas.
